title: Add links to a story or an architectural enabler with a reusable link picker
prompt:
# Story: Add links to a story or an architectural enabler with a reusable link picker

- **Story**: XXX-link-picker
- **Created**: 2026-11-09
- **Status**: Draft
- **Demo**: open an architectural enabler, press "Add link", check a driver and a story in the list, see their chips appear under "Linked to"
  at once, then open the same list from the prompt and from a test screen that links something else, and see that it is one component.

## Story

As a team member, I want to link a story or an architectural enabler to the drivers, ADRs, enablers and stories that shape it, with a link
picker that I can find in the file panel and in the prompt, so that the connections are kept with the document and used by the AI and by
the sync. As a developer, I want the picker to be **one React component that knows nothing of the builder**, so that any other component can
reuse it with its own options.

## What this is about

A **link** is a stable reference from a story or an enabler to another document: `driver:constraints`, `adr:0006`,
`enabler:0001-set-up-...` or `story:001-...`. An enabler also has the ADRs it **derives from** (`derivesFrom`), which are links of a kind.

The spike has a `LinkPicker` and a `RefChip` that do this, but they import the builder's own kinds, headings and the rule "only an Accepted
ADR" (`catalog.ts`, `generate.ts`). This story **splits it in two**:

| Part | Knows about | Lives in |
|---|---|---|
| **The component**: `LinkPicker` (the button, the list) and `LinkChip` (a chip) | nothing of the builder: it draws the groups and options it is given | presentation, shared by any screen |
| **The builder's rules**: which options a story or an enabler may be offered, in which groups, which are locked | kinds, headings, Accepted ADRs, "not itself", "an enabler keeps one ADR" | a view model of the builder, tested without rendering (ADR 0003) |

It also builds on `story-builder-folders.md` (the file panel), `story-architectural-enablers.md` (the prompt's Link button, story 6, and the
update of an enabler, story 7) and `story-adrs.md` (only an Accepted ADR can be newly linked).

---

# The journey

| # | The user... | What they see |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | opens an architectural enabler from the tree | its panel: "Derives from" (ADR chips), "Linked to" with a button "Add link", and "Referenced by" when something links to it |
| 2 | presses "Add link" | a list under the button, with the groups Drivers, ADRs, Architectural enablers and Stories, and a checkbox for each document |
| 3 | checks "Constraints" and "001. Sign in" | the button shows a count, and the chips "Constraints" and "001. Sign in" appear under "Linked to" at once |
| 4 | checks an ADR | its chip appears under **"Derives from"**, not under "Linked to" (for an enabler) |
| 5 | tries to uncheck the only ADR of the enabler | it cannot: the checkbox is checked and disabled, and says why |
| 6 | presses the X of a chip | the link is removed, and the box in the list is unchecked |
| 7 | presses Escape, or clicks outside | the list closes and the choice stays |
| 8 | presses a chip | that document opens in the panel |
| 9 | opens the document that was linked | its panel shows the first one under "Referenced by" |
| 10 | opens a story and presses "Add link" | the same list, with its own rules (it offers every ADR that is Accepted, and itself is not in it) |
| 11 | writes a prompt to update the enabler | the documents it links to go to the model in full |

## The file panel

```
architectural-enablers/0003-set-up-postgresql-and-flyway.md                                     (X)
(lock) Read-only here. ...
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DERIVES FROM
 [ADR 0006. Use PostgreSQL and Flyway ...] [ADR 0007. Use Spring Data JPA ...]

LINKED TO                                                                      [ (link) Add link 2 ]
 [Constraints (x)] [001. Sign in (x)]
 (or) Not linked to any driver, ADR, enabler or story yet.

REFERENCED BY
 [AE-0004. Set up the OpenAPI document]
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 (the Markdown, rendered or source)
```

```
 [ (link) Add link 2 ]
 +----------------------------------+
 | DRIVERS                          |
 | [x] Constraints                  |
 | [ ] Core Functionality           |
 | ADRS                             |
 | [x] ADR 0006. Use PostgreSQL ... |   <- locked when it is the last ADR of an enabler
 | [ ] ADR 0011. Use TypeScript ... |
 | ARCHITECTURAL ENABLERS           |
 | [ ] AE-0001. Set up the front... |
 | STORIES                          |
 | [x] 001. Sign in                 |
 +----------------------------------+
```

---

## Acceptance tests

The component (checked with no builder at all, with options made up by the test)

- [ ] **Given** a `LinkPicker` with a label, **Then** it shows one button with a link icon and that label (the default is "Link"), a pill with
  a thin border, with `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded="false"`.
- [ ] **Given** options selected, **Then** the button shows a small round count of the selected options that are in its groups, and none when
  the count is 0. A selected value that is in no group is not counted.
- [ ] **Given** the button, **When** the user presses it, **Then** a list opens (`role="dialog"`, named "Choose what to link"),
  `aria-expanded="true"`, and **When** the user presses it again, **Then** it closes.
- [ ] **Given** the list, **Then** it shows the groups in the order they were given, each a `fieldset` with its title as a small upper-case
  legend, and, for each option, a checkbox and its label cut with "..." when long (the full label as a tooltip). A group with no option is
  not shown.
- [ ] **Given** no group, or groups with no option, **Then** the list says "Nothing to link yet."
- [ ] **Given** an option, **When** the user checks it, **Then** the component calls `onChange` once with the selection plus that option at
  the end. **When** the user unchecks it, **Then** it calls `onChange` with the selection without it, in the same order.
- [ ] **Given** the component is **controlled**, **Then** it keeps no selection of its own: the checkboxes show what `selected` says, and a
  parent that ignores `onChange` leaves them as they were.
- [ ] **Given** an option that is **locked** with a reason, **Then** its checkbox is checked, disabled, and has the reason as its tooltip, it
  cannot be unchecked with the mouse or the keyboard, and it counts as selected.
- [ ] **Given** the list is open, **When** the user presses Escape, clicks (or presses) anywhere outside the button and the list, or presses
  the button again, **Then** it closes and the selection stays.
- [ ] **Given** the list opens from the keyboard (Enter or Space on the button), **Then** the focus moves to the first checkbox, Tab and
  Shift+Tab move through the checkboxes, Space toggles, and **When** Escape closes it, **Then** the focus goes back to the button.
- [ ] **Given** two pickers on one page with different selections, **Then** each shows its own, and toggling in one changes nothing in the
  other.
- [ ] **Given** a custom `label`, `dialogLabel` or `emptyText`, **Then** the component shows them in place of the defaults.

Where the list appears

- [ ] **Given** the list is open, **Then** it is drawn in a portal on the page, with a fixed position, so that no panel that scrolls or
  clips (the file panel, the prompt) hides it, and it is above dialogs.
- [ ] **Given** the button, **Then** the list is 320 px wide (or the window's width less 16 px when that is smaller), starts at the left of the
  button, and never goes closer than 8 px to an edge of the window.
- [ ] **Given** `placement` "down" (the default), **Then** the list opens below the button, and opens above only when there is less than
  200 px below and more room above. **Given** `placement` "up", **Then** it opens above when there are at least 160 px above or more room
  above than below.
- [ ] **Given** the list, **Then** it is at most 320 px high (less when there is less room), and it scrolls inside.
- [ ] **Given** the list is open, **When** the window is resized or anything on the page scrolls, **Then** the list is placed again by the
  button.

The chip

- [ ] **Given** a `LinkChip` with a label, an icon and a colour, **Then** it shows a pill with the icon and the label, cut with "..." when
  long, in that colour.
- [ ] **Given** it has an `onOpen`, **Then** the label is a button, underlined on hover and on focus. **Given** it has an `onRemove`, **Then** a
  small X button named "Remove link to <label>" shows. **Given** it has neither, **Then** it is plain text.

The builder's rules (the view model, checked without rendering)

- [ ] **Given** the documents of a project and a target (a story or an enabler), **Then** the groups are, in this order, "Drivers", "ADRs",
  "Architectural enablers" and "Stories", and a group with no option is left out.
- [ ] **Given** the target, **Then** it is not in its own list, so a document can never link to itself.
- [ ] **Given** the ADRs, **Then** only an Accepted ADR is offered. **Given** an ADR that is already linked and is **no longer** Accepted,
  **Then** it is still offered, checked, so that it can be unlinked.
- [ ] **Given** the drivers, **Then** every driver is offered, written or not.
- [ ] **Given** a consumer that hides a kind (the prompt of an enabler hides ADRs, because it chooses them as chips), **Then** that kind is not
  in the groups and not in the count.
- [ ] **Given** an enabler with exactly one ADR it derives from, **Then** that ADR is offered **locked**, with the reason "An enabler
  implements at least one ADR." **Given** it has two or more, **Then** none is locked.
- [ ] **Given** a story, **Then** it has no locked option, and its ADRs are ordinary links.

In the file panel of a story and of an enabler

- [ ] **Given** an open story or enabler, **Then** its panel has the heading "Linked to" with the button "Add link" on its right (the label
  "Add link"), the chips of its links under it, and, while it has none, the line "Not linked to any driver, ADR, enabler or story yet."
- [ ] **Given** an open **enabler**, **Then** the picker's checked options are the ADRs it derives from **and** its links. **When** the user
  checks an ADR, **Then** it is added to the enabler's ADRs and its chip appears under "Derives from". **When** the user checks anything
  else, **Then** it is added to its links and its chip appears under "Linked to".
- [ ] **Given** an open **story**, **When** the user checks an ADR, **Then** its chip appears under "Linked to", with the others.
- [ ] **Given** a link was added or removed, **Then** it is kept at once: there is no Save, the text of the document is not touched, and the
  panel, the count on the button and the checkboxes all change in the same moment.
- [ ] **Given** the chips of "Linked to", **Then** they are in the order they were linked, each with the icon and colour of its kind (driver
  indigo, ADR amber, enabler green, story blue), and each has an X. **When** the user presses the X, **Then** that link is removed and
  its checkbox is unchecked. **When** the user presses the label, **Then** that document opens.
- [ ] **Given** the chips of "Derives from", **Then** they open their ADR when pressed and have no X: an ADR is taken away in the picker.
- [ ] **Given** a link to a document that does not exist any more, **Then** no chip shows for it and nothing fails.
- [ ] **Given** a driver or an ADR is open (they are immutable), **Then** its panel has no "Add link" and no "Linked to".
- [ ] **Given** any document that something links to (a driver, an ADR, an enabler or a story), **Then** its panel shows "Referenced by" with a
  chip for each document that links to it or derives from it, and each chip opens that document. **Given** a link was just added from
  another document, **Then** the open panel shows it at once.
- [ ] **Given** the page is reloaded, **Then** the links and the ADRs of each document are still there. **Given** two projects, **Then** each
  keeps its own.

Reuse by the prompt, and by a third screen

- [ ] **Given** the prompt that creates an enabler (`story-architectural-enablers.md`, story 6), **Then** its "Link" button is this component,
  with the label "Link", the ADRs hidden, its list opening below or above as `placement` says, and the chips above the box built from
  `LinkChip` with an X. Every test of that story still passes.
- [ ] **Given** a test screen that has nothing to do with the builder and gives the component its own groups ("Colours", "Sizes") and its own
  selection, **Then** the component works as above, shows only those groups, and shows nothing of drivers, ADRs, enablers or stories.
- [ ] **Given** the builder, the prompt and the test screen on screen at once, **Then** each keeps its own selection.

What the links do

- [ ] **Given** the user linked a driver to the open enabler, **When** the user then sends a change in the prompt
  (`story-architectural-enablers.md`, story 7), **Then** the request's "Linked documents" has that driver in full.
- [ ] **Given** a link, **Then** the documents it connects are in the same sync (`story-git-integration.md`): the sync of one covers the other.

## Business rules and constraints

- **The component is generic.** `LinkPicker` and `LinkChip` receive groups, options, a selection, locked options, labels and handlers. They
  import nothing from the builder, the catalog, the ADRs or the drivers, and they have no rule about kinds. They are views (ADR 0003): they
  render and forward events.
- **The rules belong to the builder.** Which options a document is offered, in what order, which are locked, and how a checked ADR is stored
  are decided by a view model, which has its own tests and no React.
- A link is a **stable reference** made from the name of the file (`driver:constraints`, `adr:0006`, `enabler:0001-set-up-...`,
  `story:001-...`), never from a random id, so that it means the same on every machine.
- A document **cannot link to itself**. Links may go both ways between two documents, and a chain may loop: the picker does not check.
- **Only an Accepted ADR can be newly linked** (`story-adrs.md`). One that was linked and stopped being Accepted stays linked and can be
  unlinked.
- **An enabler always derives from at least one ADR.** Its last ADR cannot be unchecked in the picker.
- For an enabler, ADRs are stored in `derivesFrom` and everything else in `links`. For a story everything is in `links`.
- Adding or removing a link changes **only** the links (and the ADRs). It does not change the text, the title or the dates of the document.
- Drivers and ADRs are immutable in the builder, so they have no links of their own. They only show who refers to them.
- A link goes to the AI in full text (`story-architectural-enablers.md`, stories 6 and 7) and widens what a sync covers (`story-git-integration.md`).
- Everything is kept in the browser in the spike (`localStorage`, per project), and in the repository as `links` and `derivesFrom` in the
  document's `meta.json`, sorted.

## Out of scope

- Linking from a driver or an ADR, and any link to something that is not a driver, an ADR, an enabler or a story (a file, a URL).
- A search box, a filter or groups that can be folded in the list. The list scrolls.
- A rule about which kinds may link to which: any story or enabler may link to any other document, and loops are allowed.
- Warning about the effect of a link on the sync or on what the AI reads, and a graph of the links.
- Deleting a story or an enabler (the spike removes the links to it from the others; that belongs to deleting).
- Moving the whole builder to the final frontend layers. Only the picker, the chip and their view model are built here.

## Tasks

- [ ] **Write the component's tests first** (Jest and React Testing Library), with made-up groups: the button and its count, open and close
  (button, Escape, outside), the checkboxes and `onChange`, controlled, locked, empty, the keyboard and the focus, two pickers, and the
  placement (with `getBoundingClientRect`, the window size and the scroll mocked).
- [ ] Build `LinkPicker` as a view in the presentation layer: the props of the Reference, the portal, the fixed position and its recompute on
  resize and scroll, the closing rules, the focus, and the colours and classes of the spike.
- [ ] Build `LinkChip` (icon, label, colour, optional open, optional remove with its label).
- [ ] Build the builder's view model, `linkChoices`: kind order and headings, not itself, the Accepted-ADR rule with "already linked stays",
  hidden kinds, the locked last ADR of an enabler, and the count. Test it without rendering.
- [ ] Build the sections of the file panel for a story and an enabler ("Derives from", "Linked to" with "Add link", the chips, the empty line)
  on top of the two, and write the links and the ADRs through the store's `patch`, without touching the text.
- [ ] Show "Referenced by" in the panel of every document that something links to (drivers and ADRs too), updating at once.
- [ ] Move the prompt's "Link" button and its chips to the shared component, without changing what the user sees, and run the tests of
  `story-architectural-enablers.md` story 6.
- [ ] Add the test screen with its own groups, to show that the component needs nothing of the builder, and keep it in the tests only.
- [ ] Delete the builder-coupled `LinkPicker.tsx` once both consumers use the shared one.
- [ ] Check by hand, in a browser, with the keyboard only, in the dark and the light theme, near the bottom and the right edge of the window.

---

# Reference

## The component, as proposed

The spike's props are `entries`, `selected`, `onChange`, `hideKinds`, `excludeRef`, `placement` and `label`. The first, fourth and fifth tie it
to the builder, so they go to the view model. The proposal:

```ts
// The component. No import from the builder.
interface LinkOption { value: string; label: string }                    // value is the reference, e.g. "adr:0006"
interface LinkGroup  { id: string; title: string; options: LinkOption[] }

interface LinkPickerProps {
  groups: LinkGroup[];                     // in the order to show; empty groups are not drawn
  selected: string[];                      // the values that are checked, in order
  onChange: (selected: string[]) => void;  // called with the whole new selection
  locked?: Record<string, string>;         // value -> reason; checked, disabled, the reason as tooltip
  label?: string;                          // button text, default "Link"
  dialogLabel?: string;                    // default "Choose what to link"
  emptyText?: string;                      // default "Nothing to link yet."
  placement?: 'up' | 'down';               // default "down"
}

interface LinkChipProps {
  label: string;
  icon: ComponentType<{ size?: number; className?: string }>;
  tone: string;                            // the classes that colour the pill
  onOpen?: () => void;
  onRemove?: () => void;                   // shows the X named `Remove link to ${label}`
}
```

```ts
// The builder's view model. It knows the kinds and the rules.
function linkChoices(input: {
  entries: Entry[];
  target: Entry | null;          // the document being linked, left out of its own list; null when it does not exist yet
  selected: string[];            // links plus, for an enabler, its ADRs
  hideKinds?: EntryKind[];       // the prompt of an enabler hides 'adr'
}): { groups: LinkGroup[]; locked: Record<string, string> };

function applyLinkSelection(target: Entry, refs: string[]): { links: string[]; derivesFrom?: string[] };
//  enabler: derivesFrom = the "adr:" refs, links = the others.   story: links = refs (no derivesFrom).
```

## What the picker looks like in the spike

## What changes from the spike

- **The component no longer knows the builder.** It takes `groups`, `locked` and the labels. The kind order, the headings, "not itself", the
  Accepted-ADR rule and the hidden kinds go to the view model.
- **A locked option is new.** The spike lets the file panel uncheck every ADR of an enabler, which leaves it with none and breaks the rule
  that it implements at least one.
- **Keyboard and focus are new.** The spike does not move the focus into the list or back to the button.
- **The tooltip of a long label is new.**
- **"Referenced by" for drivers and ADRs.** In the spike the panel already shows it for any document, but `story-builder-folders.md` left it
  out of the read-only panels until something could link. Here it comes back.
- **The enabler's panel gets "Add link".** `story-architectural-enablers.md` (stories 3 and 7) leaves an approved enabler without it; this
  story adds it, still with no manual editing of the text.

## Spike details worth keeping in mind

- The count in the spike is the selected values that are entries whose kind is not hidden. For an enabler's file it counts the ADRs it
  derives from too, because they are in `selected`.
- The list repositions with `position: fixed`, on `resize` and on `scroll` with `capture: true`, so a scroll in any container moves it.
- The list closes on `mousedown` outside, not on `click`, so a drag that starts inside and ends outside keeps it open.
- The chips of an enabler's "Linked to" are `entry.links`, and its X calls `onLinksChange(entry.links.filter(...))` with no second argument, so
  the ADRs it derives from are left alone.
- Chips follow the order of `links` in the store. A sync writes `links` sorted and reads them back sorted, so after a download the chips can
  change order.
- A story's ADR links are ordinary `links`; they reach the model as "linked". An enabler's reach it as "derives from".
- The picker's `onChange` receives the whole list. The caller decides what to do with the ADR refs, which is how an enabler splits them.
- `removeItem` takes a deleted story or enabler out of the other documents' `links`. It does not touch `derivesFrom`, because a used ADR
  cannot be removed.
- The prompt auto-links the **cross** enablers to a new story, once each, so that one the user took out does not return. That is the prompt's,
  not the picker's.
- The spike has no test for `LinkPicker`.

## Something to decide

1. **Where the component lives and what it is called.** `LinkPicker` and `LinkChip` in the shared part of `presentation/` is proposed. The
   frontend layout of ADR 0003 has no folder yet for shared views.
2. **`value` or `ref`.** The component calls the reference `value`, so that it is not about documents. The builder calls it `ref`. A thin
   mapping in the view model is the price.
3. **Is the locked ADR rule the picker's to show, or the panel's to enforce?** The story has the view model lock it and the picker show it. If
   other consumers need "at least one of any group", `locked` is not enough and a `minimum` per group would be.
4. **A search box.** With many stories the list is long. A filter field at the top would help, and is out of scope here.
5. **Kinds that may link.** Any story or enabler may link to any document, including loops (A links B and B links A). If loops confuse the
   sync or the model's context, the picker is where to stop them.
6. **Moving focus into the list** changes how the prompt's Link button behaves when the box has the focus: the focus leaves the box. The
   story accepts that for the sake of the keyboard.
7. **Size.** The story holds the component, the view model and two consumers. If it does not fit one iteration, the component with its tests
   and the test screen come first, then the view model and the file panel, then the prompt.

tasks.text: Write Jest tests for `LinkPicker` using React Testing Library with made-up groups: button rendering and count, open/close (button press, Escape, outside click), checkboxes and `onChange`, controlled mode, locked options, empty state, keyboard navigation and focus, two independent pickers, and portal positioning (mock `getBoundingClientRect`, window size and scroll).
